headline: 4 arrested after youths carrying RJD flags tear down PM Modi posters on Nitish Setu in Bihar
content: PATNA: Four people have been arrested for allegedly tearing posters and banners put up ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Bihar's Vaishali district for the inauguration of the 'Nitish Setu', police said on Sunday.An FIR was registered at Rustampur police station following a complaint by the Raghopur block development officer (BDO). It names 11 people and more than 100 unidentified persons, police said.Modi inaugurated the bridge, named after former Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar, on Saturday. Posters and banners featuring the prime minister had been put up along the bridge ahead of his visit.Videos circulating on social media purportedly showed groups of locals, including children carrying RJD flags, tearing down posters featuring Modi."Following a complaint lodged by the Raghopur BDO on Saturday evening, an FIR was registered, and four people have been arrested," Hajipur SDO Vishal Kumar said.Police are examining the video footage to identify and arrest the remaining accused, he added.(With inputs from PTI)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Patna | Silver Rate in Patna | Bank Holidays in Patna | Public Holidays in Patna | Patna AQI | Weather in Patna | Petrol Price in Patna | Diesel Price in Patna | CNG Price in Patna | LPG Price in PatnaStay updated with the latest Patna news. headline: 'Just another jumla': Shama Mohamed takes dig at PM Modi over Pakistan minister's visit
content: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Shama Mohamed on Sunday accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of diluting his government's stated position on Pakistan after sharing a video showing Union minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat interacting with Pakistani ministers. She questioned the BJP's engagement with Pakistani leaders and contrasted it with the Congress stand that there should be no dialogue with Islamabad until it stops supporting terrorism in India.In a post on X, Mohamed alleged that Shekhawat, a minister in Modi's cabinet, had shared a meal with a Pakistani minister who had made remarks about "cutting off hands". She also took a swipe at the prime minister's slogan, "blood and water cannot flow together"."The minister in PM Modi's cabinet, Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, enjoyed a meal with the Pakistani minister who made remarks of “cutting off hands”. Narendra Modi has turned “blood and water cannot flow together” into just another jumla. Proud of my leader, LoP Rahul Gandhi Ji, who clearly stated that there can be no conversation with Pakistan until it stops supporting terrorism in India," she said.The video shared by Mohamed shows BJP leaders interacting with Pakistani ministers. In the clip, a BJP leader can be heard saying, "I am going to Pakistan with my daughter. I will be back."Mohamed also praised leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, for maintaining that India should not engage in talks with Pakistan until it ends its support for terrorism.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: 'Destroyed credibility of polls': Congress alleges gaps in voting data across 200 seats in Lok Sabha poll
content: NEW DELHI: Congress on Sunday stepped up its attack on the Centre, alleging that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah, through Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, had "destroyed" the credibility of Indian elections.In a post on X, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh reiterated the party's demand for Kumar's resignation, saying PM Modi and Shah must be held accountable for "vote chori"."An investigation has revealed that ECI's internal records are missing for voters who voted after 5 pm in 200 seats in Maharashtra, Haryana and Jammu and Kashmir in 2024. The returning officer's reports contain no figures for the final hour of polling," he wrote.Ramesh claimed that the number of votes polled was supposed to be tallied every two hours to prevent manipulation, but alleged that this procedure was not followed.He also questioned the increase in voter turnout recorded after 5 pm, citing Maharashtra, where the final turnout was 76 lakh votes higher than the figures reported at 5 pm."These late evening votes have already been suspect for bogus voting: in Maharashtra, the final turnout was 76 lakh votes higher than (the figures) reported at 5 pm. How is this possible? For one assembly, Kopri-Pachpakhadi, it means one vote was cast every 15 seconds at each booth for a full hour," Ramesh said."The Modi-Shah duo, through CEC Gyanesh Kumar, have destroyed the credibility of India's elections. They must be held accountable for this grave crime against our democracy. The CEC must resign, and the duo must answer for vote chori," he added.Meanwhile, Congress has announced a series of programmes to step up its campaign against alleged electoral irregularities.The party will organise 'Samvidhan Raksha (Save Constitution)' marches across states on November 26, observed as Constitution Day. It will also launch a booth-level verification drive to check deleted voter names and hold village-level 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao (Save Elections, Save India)' chaupals.In a circular issued to Pradesh Congress Committee presidents, general secretaries, in-charges and other key office bearers, Congress general secretary (organisation) K C Venugopal said state committees would organise 'Samvidhan Raksha' marches on November 26.Ahead of the marches, Congress workers will undertake a 'Vote Rakshak' campaign, visiting every polling booth to verify the names of voters whose names have been deleted from electoral rolls.From November 29 to December 15, the party will organise village-level 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao' chaupals based on the findings of the verification campaign.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Three arrested for tearing PM’s posters on Nitish Setu
content: Patna: Three people were arrested on Sunday on charges tearing posters of Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Nitish Setu, while an FIR was registered against 11 named accused and 100 to 150 unidentified persons in connection with the incident.Police in Vaishali district intensified action after a video showing around 100 youths tearing posters and a cut-out of PM Modi on the newly inaugurated Kachhi Dargah-Bidupur six-lane bridge across the Ganga went viral on Saturday night, shortly after its inauguration.Based on a statement from the Raghopur block development officer (BDO), an FIR was registered at Rustampur police station against the 11 named accused and 100 unidentified people. Rustampur SHO Kumar Abhishek said, “Three accused have been arrested and sent to judicial custody, while others are being identified using viral social media videos.”The incident took place around half-an-hour after the bridge was inaugurated. Earlier this month, the state govt named it Nitish Setu in recognition of former CM Nitish Kumar’s contribution.The video showed a group of youths tearing Modi’s posters and leaving his cut-out partly knocked down. They were seen raising slogans in support of RJD chief Lalu Prasad and party’s working president Tejashwi Prasad Yadav. One youth was seen carrying an RJD flag tied to a stick. Some had arrived on motorcycles parked by the roadside on the bridge. Around six policemen were seen asking them to stop and trying to disperse them.The incident triggered a war of words between BJP and RJD functionaries.BJP spokesman Neeraj Kumar Sharma criticised RJD and its workers, saying they had not changed and remained “the goondas and ruffians”.Former MLA and BJP spokesman Prem Ranjan Patel said PM Modi had gifted the bridge to people in flood-affected Raghopur, represented by Tejashwi in the assembly, and surrounding areas. “The people of the area will defeat Tejashwi in the next election,” he said, alleging RJD was opposed to development.RJD spokesman Chitranjan Gagan denied the youths were party workers. “They, in fact, were local youths who were angry with PM Modi and the central govt for various reasons. The PM, standing on the bridge, had waved his ‘gamcha’ towards them,” he said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Patna | Silver Rate in Patna | Bank Holidays in Patna | Public Holidays in Patna | Patna AQI | Weather in Patna | Petrol Price in Patna | Diesel Price in Patna | CNG Price in Patna | LPG Price in PatnaStay updated with the latest Patna news. headline: '90 seats, one crore votes': Revanth Reddy sets Congress' 2028 Telangana target
content: NEW DELHI: Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy on Sunday expressed confidence that the Congress would return to power in the state by winning 90 of the 119 Assembly seats in the 2028 elections. Addressing the party's Political Affairs Committee (PAC) meeting in Hyderabad, he said the Congress leadership was preparing a strategy to strengthen the organisation and secure another term in office."Congress will secure 90 seats with one crore votes in the next assembly elections", the CM asserted.Reddy also told the newly-appointed AICC in-charge of party affairs in Telangana, BM Sandeep, that the state Congress should work towards making Rahul Gandhi the prime minister.He said Telangana would contribute 15 Lok Sabha seats to the Congress in the 2029 general elections, provided the total number of constituencies in the state remained at 17."You have to convey our consensus to Kharge ji, Rahul ji and Sonia ji," he told Sandeep.Revanth Reddy targets BRS over 'false propaganda'The chief minister also criticised the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS), accusing its leadership of spreading false narratives against the Congress government in an attempt to return to power.Taking a dig at BRS leaders over their recent protest outside the Assembly, where they took off their shirts after being stopped by the police, Reddy said, "BRS leaders took off their shirts outside the Assembly building recently (when they were stopped by police), and now their trousers will be removed.Warns Congress leaders against public criticismAgainst the backdrop of criticism from some ruling party leaders over his government, Reddy warned Congress members against making negative remarks about the government in public."We are closely observing everyone’s behaviour and the way they speak. The party has complete information on what each leader says in public and in private," he said.He added that leaders who remained aligned with the party's position would receive organisational and other posts in due course.Says Congress could have formed government at Centre in 2024Recalling the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Reddy said he had correctly predicted that the BJP would not cross 240 seats.He argued that had the BJP won 25 fewer seats, and the Congress secured 25 more, the Congress would have formed the government at the Centre.Reddy also recalled that former prime minister Indira Gandhi represented Medak in Telangana as a Lok Sabha member when she was assassinated in 1984. He said the state Congress should now resolve to make Rahul Gandhi the prime minister.Government preparing drought action planThe chief minister said the state government would reach out to people directly after the Sankranti festival in January 2027.He also said the government was preparing an action plan to address possible drought conditions caused by the adverse impact of the El Niño phenomenon.Reddy highlighted the welfare schemes being implemented by his government and recalled the challenges faced by Congress workers during the previous BRS regime.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: 'Mandal adhyakhsh is enough for you': Nitin Nabin rubbishes Rahul Gandhi's debate challenge to PM Modi
content: NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party president Nitin Nabin on Sunday launched a broadside against Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, accusing him of making statements and walking away instead of raising issues on the floor of Parliament.While addressing a Booth Karyakarta Sammelan in Chandigarh, Nabin challenged Rahul's call for a debate with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and said that even a BJP mandal president was capable of debating him."He (Rahul Gandhi) comes, makes statements and then runs away from the battlefield. He does not have the courage to speak on the floor of Parliament," Nabin said."He posts a video challenging PM Modi to debate. Even a BJP mandal adhyakhsh is enough to debate you. There is no need for PM Modi to face you," Nabin added.Nabin also accused Congress of prioritising its own families and contrasted its governance with the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system introduced under the Modi government.Referring to the earlier remark about the leakage of funds meant for the poor, Nabin said the DBT mechanism has ensured that the entire amount reaches beneficiaries directly."Congress only thinks about their own families. Their father used to say that if one rupee is sent from Delhi, only 15 paise reaches the account of the poor. The country is fortunate to have a Prime Minister like Narendra Modi. After that, if one rupee is sent from Delhi, only one rupee reaches the account of the poor. People ask what has changed since 2014. I want to tell them that DBT is the biggest achievement," he said.This comes as Rahul has made several public calls for PM Modi to face him in an open debate. He had earlier claimed that it would take him just five minutes to establish that the prime minister was a "traitor".In a series of posts and videos shared on X last week, Rahul also challenged PM Modi to debate allegations concerning foreign influence, national security and who was anti-national.In one video, he said 24 hours had passed since he first issued the challenge and urged the prime minister to choose any venue. He proposed that the discussion take place in front of the media and the country's youth, with both leaders seated across a table and PM Modi choosing the moderator or judge. Rahul had suggested Bhagwat for the role.In another post, the Congress leader renewed the challenge while responding to PM Modi's 'Dimagi Naxal' remarks. Addressing CRPF personnel who had attended the Prime Minister's Diwali event in Bastar, he claimed their expressions suggested they did not agree with PM Modi's comments."Your faces said it all: you didn't buy the PM's lies. He called us Naxals," Rahul wrote.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Indo-Canadian ex-cabinet minister elected Ontario Liberal Party leader | World News
content: A former Indo-Canadian cabinet minister was elected on Saturday to lead the Liberal Party in Ontario, Canada’s most populous province.Navdeep Bains, considered a close crony of former Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, eked out a narrow victory in the final round of voting in Toronto by provincial Liberals. He garnered the majority with 50.3 per cent support in the third round during the party convention.Greeting those in the audience after the election, Bains that may have been “the end of a leadership race” but it was “just the beginning of our campaign” to end of the rule of the Conservative Party, which has been in power in the province since 2018. The Liberals have lost thee consecutive elections to the ruling party and Bains will be the fourth leader in nine years to oppose Ontario’s Premier (equivalent of a Chief Minister) Doug Ford.Bains was an MP from 2004 and 2011representing Mississauga—Brampton South, and returned to the House of Commons in 2015 from the riding of Mississauga—Malton when the Liberals swept to power in Ottawa in 2015. Considered a key supporter of Trudeau, particularly in the seat-rich Greater Toronto Area or GTA, Bains became a Cabinet Minister and held various portfolios before he opted out of Federal politics in January 2021. At the time of his resignation, he was Minister of Innovation, Science and Industry.Bains conceded the work ahead of him and the party would be “hard.”While Ford congratulated Bains on his election on X, the ruling party made it clear his ties to Trudeau would become a political weapon given the ex-PM’s extreme unpopularity across the county.The agency Canadian Press cited Ontario Cabinet Minister Graham McGregor as saying, “Certainly, in my region in Peel, we remember well when he was one of the biggest supporters of Justin Trudeau, not only as Prime Minister but when he was running for Liberal leader in the first place.” He added, “So we know that connection very well. I think Ontarians know that well.”Also working against him will be the anti-immigrant sentiment that has infected Canada over the past couple of years, with the main target being those of Indian origin, especially Sikhs, as they comprise the most visible of minorities.Of course, Bains may have some time to overcome those liabilities as the next provincial election is not schedule till 2030.

headline: RJD supporters tear down posters near Nitish Setu inaugurated by PM Modi in Vaishali; 3 held | India News
content: Hours after Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the six-lane Nitish Setu across the Ganga in Vaishali on Saturday, a group of people identified as Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) supporters created a commotion on the newly inaugurated bridge.Videos posted on social media show some youth tearing down posters and banners of the Prime Minister and the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA), waving RJD flags and raising slogans in support of party leaders Lalu Prasad and Tejashwi Prasad Yadav.Also read: Akhilesh insists on ‘winnability’, Congress on ‘issues’ ahead of seat talks for 2027 UP electionsHoardings featuring PM Modi pulled down, banners trampled The disruption, which lasted nearly 40 minutes according to accounts, unfolded after the formal ceremony. Footage circulating widely shows young men pulling down large hoardings featuring Modi, some trampling banners under foot, and moving about on motorcycles while police personnel stood nearby. Certain clips also capture abusive language and gestures directed at the Prime Minister. The bridge had been thrown open to the public shortly after Modi’s departure. Vaishlali superintendent of police (SP) Shubhank Mishra said the police have detained three youths, hailing from Jafrabad tola of Rurstanmpur area, for creating ruckus and obstructing the administrative works. “Other trouble mongers are being identified from the videos and raids are being conducted to nab them,” Mishra told HT.The 9.76-km main span of the cable-stayed structure, part of a roughly 19.7-km project including approach roads, connects Kacchi Dargah in Patna district with Bidupur in Vaishali. Built at an estimated cost of ₹4,280 crore, it is expected to ease pressure on the Mahatma Gandhi Setu and improve links between north and south Bihar. Modi dedicated the bridge as a tribute to former chief minister Nitish Kumar’s contribution to the state. The visit also marked one year of the NDA government under chief minister Samrat Choudhary. Nitish Kumar, who met the Prime Minister at the airport, did not attend the inauguration event itself.Also read: Protocol lapse: Owaisi gets guard of honour meant for Supreme Court judge in Saharanpur, probe orderedBJP, RJD trade barbsThe episode quickly turned political. BJP spokesperson Neeraj Kumar Sharma accused the RJD of preferring disruption over development. “While the government is delivering development, the RJD is engaging in disruption and creating a ruckus,” he said. “The people of Bihar want bridges and progress, not politics centred around tearing down posters.”From the RJD side, MP Sudhakar Singh defended the action as a legitimate protest. He argued that the bridge had already been inaugurated earlier and that large sums had been spent on a second ceremony essentially to rename it. The posters and banners, he claimed, had been put up “in a fraudulent manner.” Earlier, leader of the opposition Tejashwi Yadav had questioned the repeated inauguration of the same project and the decision to name it Nitish Setu, suggesting it sent a message that the JD(U) leader’s political career was being closed. He had also claimed the project originated during the previous Mahagathbandhan government when he held the road construction portfolio.JD(U) leaders largely focused on defending the project’s conception and execution under Nitish Kumar’s long tenure rather than issuing detailed comments specifically on Sunday’s disturbance. Party functionaries have pointed out that the bridge was envisioned years ago to address chronic congestion on the older Ganga crossing and that credit for pushing it forward belongs to Nitish.The Nitish Setu is one of several major infrastructure projects the NDA has sought to highlight. Its opening was accompanied by the inauguration or foundation-laying of other schemes worth tens of thousands of crores. Yet the images of posters being torn down within hours of the ceremony have ensured that the bridge’s political afterlife began almost as soon as traffic started rolling across it.

headline: Himachal BJP seeks dismissal of Negi over remarks on Operation Sindoor | Hindustan Times
content: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Saturday sought the dismissal of Himachal Pradesh revenue minister Jagat Singh Negi over his alleged remarks on Operation Sindoor, the Indian armed forces and Rafale fighter jets in the state assembly, submitting a memorandum to governor Kavinder Gupta.Senior BJP leader and former cabinet minister Suresh Bhardwaj, who led the delegation, demanded that the minister’s remarks be expunged from the assembly proceedings and that an inquiry be conducted into the matter. He also demanded that Negi apologise to the people of the state and the country.Speaking with the media in Shimla, Bhardwaj alleged that Negi had made inappropriate remarks on the armed forces, Operation Sindoor and Rafale fighter jets during a discussion on an unrelated subject under Rule 67 in the assembly.Bhardwaj said it was unfortunate that such remarks had been made on the floor of the House, particularly by a minister who had taken oath under the Constitution, and alleged that the comments were unrelated to the subject being discussed.“Operation Sindoor is a matter of pride for the armed forces. It is unfortunate that a senior minister made such remarks inside the assembly,” Bhardwaj said.He said the BJP had urged the governor to ensure that the remarks were removed from the assembly record and that Negi be dismissed from the Cabinet. Reacting to chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu’s support for Negi, Bhardwaj said, “If the CM is supporting him, does it mean that he is also associated with these remarks or that the minister made them with the CM’s backing? If the CM or Negi has any proof regarding their statements on Operation Sindoor, Rafale or the armed forces, they should come out in the open and substantiate their claims with facts,” he said.Bhardwaj alleged that the minister was misusing legislative privileges by making controversial remarks on the armed forces and matters concerning national security inside the assembly.

headline: Some reluctant to credit BJP for lifting 50 crore people out of poverty: PM Modi in Gujarat | India News
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday said some individuals still hesitate to acknowledge that 50 crore people have been pulled out of poverty in the country, in an apparent dig at the Opposition.Addressing BJP workers virtually during a post-Diwali 'Sneh Milan' programme organised across all 182 assembly constituencies in Gujarat, he said the achievement reflected the success of his government's policies and efforts."All those who sacrificed their lives for independence, all those who dedicated their lives to freedom, all those who spent their youth in jails for independence, wherever their souls may be, today they must be the happiest seeing this World Bank report, thinking, 'finally, poverty is leaving my country'," he said.According to a World Bank report, India's extreme poverty rate dropped sharply to 2.6 per cent in 2023 from 27.1 per cent in 2011, with the country lifting an estimated 496 million people out of poverty."A thousand years of slavery had impoverished us; for the first time after a thousand years of slavery, 50 crore people are coming out of poverty. There can be no greater satisfaction in life than this, no greater achievement than this," Modi said.ALSO READ: PM Modi says people bought less gold on his advice, invokes Lal Bahadur Shastri: ‘India still has same character’However, he said, some people were still reluctant to acknowledge the achievement."I know many people still hesitate to say this aloud, because all of this happened during this period (BJP rule). They don't like it. Whether they like it or not, we have the satisfaction that our efforts have borne fruit," Modi said.Terming the development the beginning of a new chapter in the lives of citizens, he said coming generations would witness the country's "golden era"."Our intention is true, our policy is right, our direction is right, and there is no shortcoming in our hard work," he said.The BJP had organised the programme across all 182 assembly constituencies in Gujarat. Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel listened to the PM's virtual address in his Ghatlodia constituency.Modi said this year's Diwali was significant for him as it marked 25 years since he became Gujarat's CM in October 2001.ALSO READ: RJD supporters tear down posters near Nitish Setu inaugurated by PM Modi in Vaishali; 3 heldHe credited generations of BJP workers for supporting him in his political journey and said their hard work had enabled him to serve his home state and the country.Recalling the devastating 2001 Gujarat earthquake, Modi said his first Diwali as chief minister was spent with affected families."That day, my belief became very strong that the true happiness of festivals, the true joy of festivals, lies in lighting a lamp of hope in someone else's life," he said.Modi said the spirit of public participation had helped Gujarat overcome the devastation and transform Kutch into a new centre of hope. The reconstruction efforts subsequently spread across the state, leading to a wider transformation, he said.Recalling Gujarat's development journey, Modi said the state, once largely associated with trade, had expanded its presence in sectors such as agriculture, dairy, industries, semiconductors, petrochemicals, automobiles and green energy.He said Gujarat's economic progress had contributed significantly to the country's development and reiterated his earlier slogan of achieving national development through Gujarat's development.ALSO READ:Recalling the difficult years around 2001, he said party workers had gone door-to-door collecting 'sukhdi' (a traditional sweet) for poor families to provide them with essential nutrition. They had also arranged cattle fodder from different parts of the country during droughts and organised cattle camps, he said.The PM said public participation had helped Gujarat overcome droughts and water shortages."Campaigns to conserve water and construct check dams had gradually turned into mass movements, changing the situation in the state," he said.The prime minister also referred to the Garib Kalyan Melas launched during his tenure as the CM in 2001, saying they helped build confidence among poor families and encouraged them to come out of poverty.ALSO READ:"The experience gained from launching such programmes helped me create welfare schemes introduced by my government at the Centre after 2014," said the PM.Modi recalled that when his government started opening bank accounts for the poor, critics questioned their utility, while similar doubts were raised over the provision of LPG connections to households that could not afford cylinder refills."We kept making scheme after scheme and taking them to the last person in the queue. We proved what social justice means for those who are rightful claimants and in need. And who were the ones without bank accounts? Our Dalit families, tribal families, the oppressed and downtrodden, as well as the women," the PM said.While bank accounts were opened, gas stoves arrived in homes, and electricity connections and Ayushman cards were distributed to the needy, he said."As a result of all these schemes, 50 crore people have come out of poverty," the PM added.Modi urged BJP workers to keep national interest above party interests. He said the social harmony and unity developed in Gujarat would help the state and the country progress.He expressed confidence that Gujarat would achieve much more in the next 20 years than it had accomplished over the previous 25 years.

headline: Government taking steps to attract IT firms, boost start-up ecosystem in Himachal: CM | Hindustan Times
content: Himachal chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Saturday inaugurated the Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) Centre at Chetru, near Gaggal Airport in Kangra district set up at a cost of ₹18.29 crore.The centre is expected to support up to 20 budding entrepreneurs and generate employment opportunities for 350 to 400 persons over the next five years.The initiative is aimed at strengthening the IT ecosystem in Himachal Pradesh, attracting investments in the information technology sector and providing an environment for start-ups and budding entrepreneurs.The centre has been equipped with modern infrastructure, including plug-and-play incubation facilities, raw incubation space, manager’s cabins, a 40-seater auditorium, conference and meeting rooms, network operations centre, reception area, guest rooms and other essential facilities.The CM said that the state government was committed to developing Himachal Pradesh as an emerging destination for information technology and investment. He said that the government was taking concrete steps to attract IT companies, promote start-ups and create a conducive ecosystem for innovation and entrepreneurship.He said that the establishment of the STPI Centre at Kangra would provide local entrepreneurs and IT professionals with access to modern infrastructure and new opportunities within the state, while also generating employment for the youth.‘Govt to consider adding ‘Centenary’ prefix to Dharamshala college’s name’Sukhu also assured the Old Students’ Association (OSA) of Government College, Dharamshala, that the state government would consider adding the prefix ‘Centenary’ to the name of the prestigious institution to commemorate its 100-year journey.The CM attended a function organised by the OSA as part of the college’s centenary celebrations. During the interaction, the CM also assured the OSA that the government would sympathetically consider its demands for permanent protection of the landslide-prone Pines area and setting up an office for the association in the college.CM administers oath to newly appointed HPERC chairmanSukhu administered the oath of office and secrecy to the newly appointed chairman of the Himachal Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (HPERC), Pankaj Rai, at Dharamshala in Kangra district.The CM expressed hope that the newly appointed chairman would discharge his responsibilities with dedication, integrity and professionalism.

headline: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties to hold fresh coalition talks as Israel faces government formation deadlock | World News
content: The parties of caretaker Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot are set to hold a new round of talks on Sunday over whether to form a coalition government.Delegations from Eisenkot's Yashar party and Netanyahu's Likud are to meet at 1:00 pm (1100 GMT) in a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, for a second consecutive Sunday of negotiations, according to TV news Channel 14.Also Read: Israel election: The numbers, alliances and 61-seat mark that decides who governsA former army chief of staff, Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, with the possibility of a 14?day extension, after October elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority.His bloc nevertheless remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra?Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud.On Saturday, Yashar presented the resumption of talks as "a genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government", saying that Eisenkot had asked his representatives to explore all options.But Likud immediately laid down several conditions for its participation in a unity government, a formula backed by Netanyahu.Among other things, it demands an end to "all personal attacks and incitement to hatred" targeting the outgoing prime minister and his government.It also called for bringing together "all the parties that support the existence of the State of Israel as the nation?state of the Jewish people", without the participation of Arab parties.Also Read: The options before Israel: A Netanyahu-Eisenkot deal, a minority government or no new governmentRefusalNetanyahu and his allies regularly target Arab parties, which secured a record 19 seats in the legislature and are opposed to Netanyahu remaining in power.Likud is also demanding agreement on several major policy positions, notably rejecting the creation of a Palestinian state, maintaining Israeli control over territories in Syria, Lebanon and the Gaza Strip, and a compromise on conscription of ultra?Orthodox Jews, a particularly sensitive issue in Israel.A unity government could be based on a rotation of the prime minister role between the two men, each heading the executive in turn, a formula already tried in Israel.Eisenkot has nonetheless ruled out serving in a government led by Netanyahu.His ally Naftali Bennett, a former prime minister, also reiterated on Saturday his refusal to join a coalition with "Netanyahu or his bloc, under any circumstances".Also Read: Eisenkot gets first shot at forming Israel’s government: The next possible scenariosOn Friday, Eisenkot warned that he would not allow the talks to drag on, saying he was ready to submit to parliament an "emergency national government".Although he did not spell out how, his statements suggest a two?stage plan: the swift formation of a minority government based on the core opposition parties, and then broadening it.

headline: Congress factional rift deepens in Keralam, dissenting leaders take grievances to Kharge in Delhi | India News
content: The factional troubles within the Congress in Keralam have reached the AICC leadership in Delhi within six months of coming to power in the state with a section of leaders airing their grievances before national president Mallikarjun Kharge, leaders familiar with the matter said.A batch of leaders belonging to a prominent faction, including a Lok Sabha MP, met Kharge and relayed complaints about lack of coordination between the party and the government, the impact of delay in appointing the state unit president as well as lack of proper consultations on the appointments to various boards and corporations, said a senior leader on condition of anonymity.The leaders who met Kharge are reported to belong to the so-called 'A' group of the Congress, which was earlier led by AK Antony during his time in the state unit. After Antony's move to Delhi in the early 2000s, the faction was subsequently led by former chief minister Oommen Chandy, who passed away in July 2023. After Chandy's demise, the 'A' group had largely weakened, only to be resurrected now.ALSO READ: '₹32 crore lottery, plans to pay off mortgage and travel the world">I was shocked': Keralam woman in Canada wins ₹32 crore lottery, plans to pay off mortgage and travel the world"The factional leaders have informed the AICC that their suggestions and views are not being considered within party forums on crucial policy issues as well as appointments to boards and corporations after the UDF government came to power," the leader said. With most of the senior leaders of the state unit finding positions in the cabinet, there are also grievances about lack of internal consultations within the Congress and the larger UDF coalition. There are already internal grievances that Chief Minister VD Satheesan is taking unilateral decisions without due consultations.ALSO READ: Factions of parishioners clash at Kerala Catholic church over resignation of priest, police deployedWith current KPCC president Sunny Joseph also serving as Power Minister, there is a requirement for a full-time state president to look after organisational issues as well as keep a firm check on the government. Several district presidents have been elected as MLAs, underlining the need to reconstitute district committees and elect new presidents.The meeting of the factional leaders with Kharge comes just weeks after UDF convenor Adoor Prakash conveyed similar grievances about absence of UDF meetings and consultations to the AICC leadership. While Prakash's complaint was submitted, the AICC has not formally acted on it.Joseph told reporters on Sunday that he will hold meetings with the AICC leadership later this month when he travels to the national capital for a meeting with power ministers from all states."All issues will be discussed within a time-frame. Our view is that all major issues must be talked about (internally) before being announced by the government," Joseph said.At the same time, Rajmohan Unnithan, Lok Sabha MP from Kasaragod, underlined that there is no internal mechanism within the party currently for leaders to air their grievances."I also have a lot of complaints, but I am clinging on. VD Satheesan is a chief minister of the Congress and the UDF. If there was a (strong) party mechanism, all decisions of the State government would have been discussed. If a party faction has raised its grievances before Kharge, it certainly has a right to do so," said Unnithan.However, health minister and former KPCC president K Muraleedharan, seen as close to CM Satheesan, said the good things being done by the state governments are not being highlighted enough amid internal dissensions."The good things done by the government are being pushed behind a smoke screen. Our focus should be on highlighting the positives of the government. Every week, the CM is briefing the media about cabinet meetings. Everything is systematic," said the minister.

headline: PM Modi's call to defer gold purchase averted losses: BJP slams Congress for ‘misleading’ traders
content: <p>The BJP on Sunday said that Prime Minister <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/pm-modi">Narendra Modi's</a> call to avoid buying gold earlier in the year has saved traders from incurring losses, while demanding an apology from the Congress for describing the prime minister's call as a "death warrant" and "creating panic".</p><p>This comes after the Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) wrote to Modi, thanking him for his earlier advice to people against buying <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/gold">gold</a>.</p><p>The body said that the prime minister's advice saved lakhs of jewellers, traders and investors from huge losses as gold prices fell by Rs 65 lakh per kg, from Rs 1.90 crore to Rs 1.25 crore. </p>.<p>It also said the decline in gold prices has brought relief to families during the ongoing wedding season.</p>.PM Modi links gold price dip to his appeal, says AI cannot take away jobs of skilled workers.<p>BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari hit out at the Congress in a post on X, saying Modi appealed to the people of India to defer purchase of gold, Congress termed it a "death warrant".</p><p>"With gold prices falling globally, traders following PM Modi's advice saved Rs 65 lakh per kg of gold. The trader bodies have thanked the prime minister today," he said.</p><p>"The Congress should apologise to the traders for misleading them and creating panic," the BJP spokesperson wrote, adding, "Gandhi-Vadra family, which lived a lavish lifestyle when India's majority was poor, should take a master class in economic management and simple living from PM Modi." </p>

headline: I do not shoot arrows from behind, I am straightforward: Keralam minister Muraleedharan
content: <p>Thiruvananthapuram: <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/Kerala">Keralam</a> Health Minister K Muraleedharan on Sunday denied allegations that he had leaked details of differences within the state Cabinet, saying he was not someone who "shoots arrows from behind" and believed in straightforward functioning.</p>.<p>Responding to reporters' queries here about reports of heated exchanges between <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/v-d-satheesan">Chief Minister V D Satheesan</a> and some of his Cabinet colleagues over the appointment of Kerala Public Service Commission (PSC) members, and allegations that Muraleedharan had leaked details of the differences, he said he believed in straightforward functioning.</p>.<p>"I do not shoot arrows from behind. I am straightforward in my approach and do not indulge in such indirect attacks," he said.</p>.K Muraleedharan backs Keralam CM Satheesan, says govt will complete 5-year term.<p>"There is no need for a discussion on this now. Several good things being done by the government have been pushed into the background. Instead of giving importance to such issues, we should focus on the government's projects and ensure that the government moves forward together. That is the decision we have collectively taken," he said.</p>.<p>He also denied any lack of coordination within the Congress and the United Democratic Front (UDF).</p>.<p>"Otherwise, we would not have won 102 seats. Could the Congress have secured 102 seats if it had remained inactive? The party, the front and the government will continue to move forward together," he said.</p>.<p>He said the Cabinet had been meeting every Wednesday since the government assumed office and the chief minister had been briefing the media on Cabinet decisions, reflecting the systematic functioning of the government.</p>.Won't let anyone to 'hijack' state govt event: Keralam's Muraleedharan displeased over full rendition of Vande Mataram.<p>Differences were natural in democratic movements and could be resolved, he said, adding that the delay in finalising the PSC members' list was not significant.</p>.<p>"There was a small doubt raised by the chief minister about one name. It was resolved immediately on the same day, before he left for Delhi the next day. The list has been sent to the Governor. Once the Governor's order comes, the appointments of the four or five members will be notified," he said.</p>.<p>He also said the Congress had never received such a large share of PSC members and government pleader positions under the party quota in the past, but only negative issues were being discussed.</p>.<p>Asked about his sister Padmaja Venugopal quitting the BJP and returning to the Congress, Muraleedharan said he had already responded to the issue and did not wish to repeat his remarks.</p>.Kerala High Court says Guruvayur temple staff must treat devotees with respect, maintain calm.<p>"The KPCC president and the CM can decide on such matters. I have already said what I had to say, and there is no need for me to intervene further," he said.</p>.<p>On Ambalapuzha independent MLA G Sudhakaran, who was backed by the UDF in the Assembly election, criticising Congress leaders, Muraleedharan described him as an elder statesman whose advice was valued.</p>.<p>"He is a senior leader and we are willing to accept his suggestions. He has been making reasonable interventions on issues such as Alappuzha Medical College, and we have implemented several of his suggestions. We will consider his advice with due respect," he said.</p>.<p>On a young woman in Malappuram reportedly suffering from a kidney ailment after using a face cream promoted through Instagram, the minister cautioned people against using unapproved products sold online.</p>.<p>"People should check where such products are manufactured before applying them to their faces. There are several government-approved creams available. Applying creams does not necessarily enhance beauty. The government will take action based on complaints received," he said.</p>.<p>He clarified that such products did not come under the purview of the Food Safety Department as they were not food items.</p>.<p>Asked whether regulations would be introduced, he said the government would decide on the matter, which had recently come to its notice.</p>.<p>On the online sale of unapproved medicines, Muraleedharan said the government was considering the issue and would soon take a decision.</p>.<p>"The government is looking into this even in the absence of a specific complaint. We will not allow such medicines to be sold in this manner. If specific complaints are received about any medicines, action will be taken after examination," he said. </p>

headline: SP feared 'Jai Shri Ram', now rattled by 'Radhe Radhe: UP Deputy CM takes a dig at Akhilesh
content: <p>Lucknow: <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/keshav-prasad-maurya">Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya</a> on Sunday hit out at <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/akhilesh-yadav">Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav</a> over his remarks on the BJP's 'Radhe Radhe, Kamal Khila De' slogan, accusing the opposition party of objecting to religious chants.</p><p>In a post on X, Maurya said SP leaders, who had earlier been uncomfortable with the slogan 'Jai Shri Ram', were now taking issue with 'Radhe Radhe'.</p>.<p>"In Ayodhya, 'Jai Shri Ram' resonates, while in Braj people greet each other by saying 'Radhe Radhe'," he said.</p><p>Questioning Yadav's objection to the slogan, the deputy chief minister asked whether people in Uttar Pradesh would now need the SP chief's permission to invoke their deities.</p><p>Maurya accused the SP of pursuing appeasement politics and asserted that both 'Jai Shri Ram' and 'Radhe Radhe' would continue to be heard across the state. He also predicted that the SP would fail to return to power in the 2027 Assembly elections, claiming the BJP would retain office.</p><p>His remarks came a day after Yadav ridiculed the BJP's new slogan at a press conference at the party headquarters in Lucknow.</p>.SP chief Akhilesh Yadav mulls tie-up with smaller outfits in Uttar Pradesh polls to ‘consolidate’ OBC votes.<p>Referring to the BJP's two-day meeting in Mathura, Yadav said the party had turned to the chant because the lotus, its election symbol, was wilting.</p><p>"'Radhe Radhe' is said at the time of farewell in our tradition. It means the BJP is going to be shown the door," Yadav said, adding that voters would give the party a "grand farewell" in the next Assembly elections.</p><p>The BJP organised the brainstorming session in Mathura on November 16 and 17, with its national president Nitin Nabin attending the concluding day's proceedings.</p><p>BJP state president and Union Minister of State for Finance Pankaj Chaudhary had said the meeting opened with the slogan 'Radhe Radhe, Kamal Khila De', in keeping with Mathura's association with Lord Krishna.</p><p>Chaudhary had also expressed confidence that the BJP would secure a third consecutive term in Uttar Pradesh, following its victories in the 2017 and 2022 Assembly elections.</p>

headline: Mumbai Diary | Pawar may pitch for bigger role for Sule
content: There is speculation in Maharashtra’s power corridors that if 85-year-old leader Sharad Pawar is negotiating a deal with the BJP, it is unlikely to be small. He may not only be seeking the reunification of two NCP factions but also be bargaining for a bigger role for his daughter Supriya Sule. Buzz is that the veteran may be pitching for Maharashtra top job if the BJP is keen to bring him into the NDA. Sule’s recent shift in stand on delimitation and women’s reservation bill has fuelled such speculation. She defended delimitation, saying that the UPA government had also undertaken the exercise. Whether this signals a larger political realignment remains to be seen..Sena leader’s plan falls flat after rowShiv Sena (UBT) leader Anand Dube, who recently joined Deputy CM Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena, was keen to establish himself as one of its key spokespersons. He sought to corner the Congress and Uddhav Thackeray’s faction over references to VD Savarkar in Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, ‘Belonging’. Dube reportedly purchased a copy of the book and rehearsed his arguments before addressing the media. However, party colleague Saina NC’s controversial act of tearing a photograph of Shiv Sena founder Balasaheb Thackeray overshadowed the exercise. The incident embarrassed the Sena and shifted political narrative. Shinde reprimanded his spokespersons, particularly Saina. Dube’s attempt to launch himself as the party’s aggressive new face was pushed into the background..Rohit’s tough poser on Ajit aircraft crashNationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) leader Rohit Pawar has posed a challenge to CM Devendra Fadnavis, which many opposition politicians appear reluctant to undertake. He has chosen to confront Fadnavis over the delay in the investigation into Ajit Pawar’s death in a plane crash. He has raised questions on the Chief Minister’s links to the company that operated the aircraft. The Bharatiya Janata Party hit back, accusing Rohit of making politically motivated allegations. The buzz doing the rounds is whether Rohit will build his political career around an anti-Fadnavis plank, much as the CM once built his political identity through his opposition to Sharad Pawar, or eventually retreat under political pressure.Sudhir Suryawanshi Our correspondent in Maharashtrasuryawanshi.sudhir@gmail.com.Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: CM Shivakumar: Festival advance for government employees doubled
content: HIRIYUR: Chief Minister DK Shivakumar on Saturday announced that the festival advance given to government employees would be doubled from Rs 25,000 to Rs 50,000, and assured them that the government would positively consider their demands concerning the Old Pension Scheme (OPS) and the National Pension System (NPS). He also announced a grant of Rs 3 crore for the construction of a government employees’ association building in Hiriyur.Inaugurating the taluk government employees’ convention, felicitation programme and Kannada Rajyotsava celebrations at the Government Girls’ Pre-University College in Hiriyur, Shivakumar said the government would hold consultations with the finance department, the cabinet, office-bearers of the Congress and the committee that prepared the party’s election manifesto before taking a decision on the OPS and NPS demands.Responding to the demand for an increase in the festival advance, Shivakumar announced the decision on the spot. “The pen is in my hand, and I am making a special announcement for Hiriyur. The festival advance will be increased from Rs 25,000 to Rs 50,000,” he said. He said the government had increased the salaries of employees by 27 per cent soon after assuming office and was committed to fulfilling the assurances made in its election manifesto.Shivakumar also accepted several demands made by the employees’ association, including the construction of an employees’ community hall, renovation of the teachers’ building and resumption of the stalled construction of the employees’ building. He signed the representations submitted by the association at the venue..Public Grievance Hearing Programmes Every MonthShivakumar said all ministers would hold public grievance redressal programmes on two Saturdays every month to address people’s problems.He said he would personally visit two or three places every month to hear public grievances. “It is the respon-sibility of our government to ease people’s suffering and bring about a positive change in their lives,” he said.World Kannada Conference Next YearShivakumar said the state was considering organising a three-day World Kannada Conference next year. “We have already discussed the proposal with colleagues. Kannadigas living abroad are coming together in the name of their language, rising above caste and religious differences. We want to invite them and honour their contribution. The proposal will be discussed in the Cabinet before the programme is finalised,” he said.Centre Responsible For Fixing Sugarcane PricesResponding to the Opposition’s criticism that the government was announcing projects worth Rs 2,000 crore in Hiriyur while failing to address the concerns of cane farmers, Shivakumar said, “The Centre has not fixed the price for the last 10 years. But ministers took the initiative and held discussions with factory owners to arrive at a price,” he said..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Fresh appointments: Tanveer to be CM’s political secy, Belur Assembly chief whip
content: BENGALURU: The Congress high command has approved the names of 18 party leaders for key posts, including chiefs of various boards and corporations, in the state.Sagar MLA Belur Gopalkrishna has been appointed as government chief whip of the Legislative Assembly and MLC Manjunath Bhandari as chief whip of the Council. Narasimaraja (Mysuru) MLA Tanveer Sait has been appointed as CM’s political secretary. These leaders were among the strong contenders for cabinet berths.Anekal MLA B Shivanna has been appointed as chairman of KSPCB, Tiptur MLA K Shadakshari as chairman of Karnataka State Minerals Corporation Limited, Kollegal MLA AR Krishnamurthy as chairman of BMTC, and Raichur Rural (ST) MLA Basanagouda Daddal as chairman of Kalyana Karnataka Region Development Board.Ramdurg MLA PM Ashok Pattan has been made chairman of Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers’ Welfare Board. Sindhanuru MLA Hampanagouda Badarli has been appointed as chairman of Karnataka State Warehousing Corporation, Honnali MLA DG Shanthana Gowda as chairman of Bangalore Solid Waste Management Limited, and Tarikere MLA GH Srinivas as chairman of KSTDC.Bailhongal MLA Mahantesh Koujalagi has been appointed as chairman of Karnataka Road Development Corporation, Bagepalli MLA SN Subbareddy as chairman of MSIL, Navalgund MLA NH Konaraddi as chairman of Karnataka Agriculture Price Commission and Kalaburagi South MLA Allamprabhu Patil as chairman of Karnataka Small Scale Industries Development Corporation. These MLAs had also lobbied for cabinet berths..Congress functionaries Shyam Natekar, HC Lalith Raghav and Subhash Rathore have been appointed as chairpersons of Karnataka Spices Development Board, Karnataka Vidyuth Karkhane Limited and Karnataka Thanda Development Corporation, respectively.This is part of the damage control exercise of the Congress in view of the 2028 Assembly elections.Tanveer Sait on Saturday expressed dissatisfaction over his appointment as political secretary to the chief minister, saying the position does not suit his stature and seniority. The state government on Saturday appointed chairpersons to various boards and corporations, assigning Sait the post of political secretary to the chief minister. Sait said the position did not carry significant decision-making powers and that he was not satisfied with the offer. He said he had worked for a long time to strengthen the chief minister politically and had expected a post commensurate with his seniority. “I was confident that I would be given a position befitting my seniority. However, I have learnt that I have been appointed political secretary to the chief minister. I have not received any official communication from the chief minister’s office so far. This position is not suitable for me, and I have already conveyed that I was not interested in it. I will decide on my next course of action after hearing from the chief minister,” Sait said..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: 'PM's call to defer gold purchases saved traders from losses, Congress must apologise': BJP
content: The BJP on Sunday said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi's earlier call to defer gold purchases had saved traders from losses and demanded an apology from the Congress for describing his appeal as a "death warrant" and accusing him of creating panic.The BJP's response came after the Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) wrote to Modi, thanking him for his earlier advice urging people not to buy gold.The chamber said the prime minister's advice saved lakhs of jewellers, traders and investors from huge losses as gold prices fell by Rs 65 lakh per kg, from Rs 1.90 crore to Rs 1.25 crore. It also said the decline in gold prices has brought relief to families during the ongoing wedding season.Hitting out at the Congress, BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari, in a post on X, said when Prime Minister Modi appealed to people of India to defer purchase of gold, Congress termed it a "death warrant"."With gold prices falling globally, traders following PM Modi's advice saved Rs 65 lakh per kg of gold. The trader bodies have thanked the prime minister today," he said."The Congress should apologise to the traders for misleading them and creating panic," the BJP spokesperson wrote, adding, "Gandhi-Vadra family, which lived a lavish lifestyle when India's majority was poor, should take a master class in economic management and simple living from PM Modi.(With inputs from PTI).'You saved hard-earned capital of lakhs of families': Trade body thanks PM Modi for appeal to curb gold buys.Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: ‘BJP agents in JD(U) paving way for merger’: Prashant Kishor questions Nitish Kumar's public absence
content: Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor on Sunday alleged that “BJP agents” within the JD(U) were facilitating a merger of the regional party with the BJP and keeping its chief Nitish Kumar away from public appearances.Kishor, a former national vice-president of the JD(U), was responding to questions about Kumar's absence from a function on Saturday at which Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated a bridge named after the former Bihar chief minister in Vaishali district.“You should pose this question to Sanjay Jha (JD(U) working president) as to why Nitish Kumar, who had received the PM at Patna airport, was not present at the function in Vaishali district,” Kishor told PTI Videos.“The fact is that the JD(U) is being run by BJP agents who are paving the way for the party's merger (with the saffron outfit). To this end, they are ensuring that Nitish Kumar is kept away from the public eye,” the Bankipur MLA alleged.NDA sources, however, told PTI that Kumar was not invited to the programme as he no longer held a constitutional post after stepping down in April, and the event was a government function. They also pointed out that several JD(U) leaders, including Kumar's son Nishant, a minister, and Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Kumar Choudhary, were present at the event.A senior RJD leader, speaking on condition of anonymity, told PTI that the NDA's explanation was questionable, noting that JD(U) working president Sanjay Jha and Rashtriya Lok Morcha president Upendra Kushwaha, both Rajya Sabha MPs like Kumar, were present at the function..On Prime Minister Modi's claim that his government had lifted 50 crore people out of poverty since 2014, Kishor said the assertion was “correct” in the context of migration of Bihar's poor youth to other states for work.“While the Congress gave the slogan of 'Garibi Hatao' (poverty eradication), Modi has forced Bihar's poor youth to migrate to Gujarat and Tamil Nadu for jobs and daily wage work. In that sense, his claim is correct,” he said.Kishor also responded to Rahul Gandhi's recent remarks on India's global economic standing, saying the country's position internationally would depend on its underlying strengths.“India's global standing will improve only when its education system, healthcare, economy and military become stronger. Its position on the world stage will automatically improve once these foundations are strengthened,” he said.He further accused the government of using “Jeevika Didis” as a political cadre for the BJP and NDA, referring to their attendance at the inauguration of Nitish Setu in Vaishali.“Modi promised to make Jeevika Didis the Lakhpati Didis (women earning at least Rs 1 lakh annually). However, they have been turned into a permanent cadre of the BJP and the NDA using taxpayers' money,” Kishor alleged.Rahul Gandhi, during an interaction at Columbia University in New York earlier this week, had claimed India was facing an “economic disaster”, citing unemployment, a weakened manufacturing base and problems in the education system.(With inputs from PTI).Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: 4 skill trainees from Odisha felicitated by PM Modi at Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh
content: BHUBANESWAR : In a moment of pride, four skill trainees from government ITIs and NSTI, Bhubaneswar were felicitated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the 5th Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh at Indira Gandhi Pratishthan, Lucknow, on Saturday.They are Abhijit Das of Government ITI, Cuttack, Supritee Mohapatra of Government ITI, Puri, along with Samida Begam and Sachin Kumar from the National Skill Training Institute (NSTI), Bhubaneswar. They were felicitated by the PM in recognition of their outstanding performance in the All India Trade Test (AITT) 2026.Officials of the Skill Development and Technical Education (SDTE) department said the four achievers were among the 52 outstanding trainees from across the country who have been recognised by the prime minister for their exceptional performance in the AITT, conducted by the Directorate General of Training (DGT), Government of India.Demonstrating exceptional skill and dedication, Abhijit Das emerged as the best trainee in Eastern India in the Welder trade under the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS), securing a perfect score of 600 out of 600. Supritee Mohapatra achieved an impressive 1,194 out of 1,200 marks and was adjudged the best female trainee in the Mechanic Motor Vehicle trade, one of the highly competitive technical disciplines.Similarly, in the Craft Instructor Training Scheme (CITS) category, Samida Begam (Computer Software Applications) and Sachin Kumar (Electronics Mechanic), both from NSTI, Bhubaneswar, were recognised as the best trainees in Eastern India in their respective trades..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: DK Shivakumar Invites BJP’s BY Vijayendra To Probe CM Residence Cost
content: Chitradurga: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar on Saturday offered to constitute a five-member committee headed by BJP state president BY Vijayendra to probe the expenditure on renovating the Kumara Krupa guest house, a heritage building converted into the Chief Minister’s official residence ‘Ganga’. The offer came after Vijayendra questioned the renovation expenditure, claiming that, according to his information, around Rs 100 crore of public money had been spent on the project. Shivakumar said the committee could comprise members from the BJP, JD(S) and even Independents, and that no Congress member need be part of it. Speaking to reporters in Hiriyur, he said the committee could submit its report within a week for discussion in the Assembly during the legislature session early next month. “I am telling you, I am ready to constitute an inquiry committee under Vijayendra’s chairmanship. Who should be part of it? Not a single person from our party (Congress) is needed. Let them include members from the JD(S), BJP-NDA and, if they want, even Independents,” he said. “I will constitute a five-member committee. Let them conduct the inquiry, examine all the records and find out where and how the Rs 100 crore was spent, if that is the amount. Let them do it,” he said. “Within two days, he can decide who should be part of his team. He can choose anyone he wants. Let him select any BJP and JD(S) MLAs or MLCs and conduct the inquiry. After that, let them submit a report to the Assembly. Whatever criticism they want to make, whatever they want to say, the people of the state will know how much has been spent,” he said. “Look, I invited everyone, including Vijayendra (for lunch at the official residence). I am also an MLA, just like the other 224 MLAs. I invited everyone; leaders from all parties attended. Some people did not come; that is a different matter,” he said. On Friday, Vijayendra accused the government of extravagant spending on the renovation, which he said reportedly cost around Rs 100 crore, and claimed that questions had been raised over the tendering process. “The CM should disclose how much public money has been spent on the renovation. There are allegations that the work was carried out without a proper tender process. What was the need for such extravagant expenditure during a drought?” he had asked. Vijayendra also sought clarification on reports that contractors had been instructed to submit bills totalling only Rs 2-3 crore. Asked about the BJP’s opposition to any move by the Congress government to repeal the anti-conversion and anti-cow slaughter laws, Shivakumar said the Congress had its own principles and believed in protecting and respecting cows. “Let us see. Our party has certain principles. We protect cows and treat them with respect. There are many laws that were brought in earlier (during BJP rule). But that does not mean bringing in a law to create hatred against others. We have to protect the lives and livelihoods of people from all communities,” he said. Questioning the BJP’s stance on cow protection, he asked why there were so many big export companies in Uttar Pradesh, a BJP-ruled state. “Why are there so many big export companies in Uttar Pradesh? It is their own (BJP-ruled) state. Let them shut them down there,” he said. “We will certainly protect cows and do whatever is necessary to preserve them and show them the respect they deserve. However, in the name of such laws, we cannot allow anyone to misuse the authority,” Shivakumar said.

headline: PM Modi Condoles Demise Of BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Wadkute
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday condoled the death of BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Wadkute and said that he will be remembered for his contribution to society and service to the poor and downtrodden.Wadkute, who was elected to the Upper House earlier this year, died following a cardiac arrest at a hospital in New Delhi. "Deeply saddened by the passing of Rajya Sabha MP Shri Ramrao Wadkute ji. He will be remembered for his contribution to society and emphasis on serving the poor and downtrodden," Modi said in a post on 'X'. The prime minister said equally noteworthy were Wadkute's efforts to strengthen the BJP in Maharashtra. "My thoughts are with his family and admirers. Om Shanti," he said.

headline: Darjeeling BJP MLA’s Aide Held for Cheating WB CM’s Aides
content: Kolkata: Darjeeling BJP MLA Noman Rai's close aide Ribha Lama was arrested by the police in Siliguri on Saturday evening for allegedly duping two brothers, known for their proximity to West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, over Rs 1 crore on the pretext of giving them work contracts in the Sevoke-Rangpo railway project in the hills.Ribha was present with Mr Rai at a coffee shop in City Centre in the downtown when the cops raided the shopping mall to catch him. He was remanded in five days’ police custody by the Siliguri Sub Division Court on Sunday.Preliminary investigation revealed Ribha took more than Rs 1 crore from Shubhankar Arora and his brother Dipankar Arora, who are from Siliguri, in 2024 with the false promise. The two brothers lodged a written complaint against Ribha at the Siliguri police station on November 18.Dipankar claimed, "We were lured by him with a promise to get work under a project in Darjeeling. Later he took more than Rs 1 crore in multiple installments from us but never fulfilled the promise." On the other hand, Mr Rai called Ribha his childhood friend whom he had invited to coffee at the mall following his return to Siliguri.

headline: Bennett Backs Eisenkot For PM, Rules Out Serving Under Netanyahu
content:
Gadi Eisenkot, who is tasked with forming the next Israeli government, has invited the right-wing Likud party of caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu for coalition talks, his party said on Saturday. Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party said the talks, scheduled to begin on Sunday, reflected a "genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government".

Former military chief Eisenkot has until next month to form a government to replace Netanyahu, after the October election failed to deliver a clear majority for either bloc. Saturday's announcement comes as Eisenkot's wide-ranging camp faces divisions on whether to forge alliances with the ultra-Orthodox parties, or the Arab-majority lists, or whether to form a national unity government with Netanyahu's bloc.

"In an effort to pursue every option for forming a new government, Yashar Chair Gadi Eisenkot has instructed the party's negotiating team to invite its Likud counterparts to a marathon series of talks beginning with the meeting already scheduled for tomorrow," the party said in a statement.

Former prime minister Naftali Bennett, an important figure in Eisenkot's camp, on Saturday called for a "Zionist unity government headed by Eisenkot" and said his party would refuse to join up with Netanyahu or his bloc. Netanyahu has been pushing hard for a national unity government, which he says is needed to guarantee Israel's security.

Shortly after Eisenkot's announcement, Likud laid out its position on forming such a government with Eisenkot's bloc, including demands to halt "all personal attacks and incitement" as well as political "boycotts" against Netanyahu and the government. Eisenkot has indicated he would be open to forming a government with members of Netanyahu's Likud, but has previously ruled out serving in a government led by Netanyahu himself.

Likud also called for a joint declaration committing to a unity government including "all parties that support the existence of the State of Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people" and without the participation of Arab parties.

Netanyahu and his allies have repeatedly criticised leaders of Arab parties for refusing to describe Hamas as a "terror group" following its October 7, 2023 attack on Israel. All leaders of Arab parties have condemned the attack.

Likud proposed a set of guidelines for a unity government including an agreement that Israel is the nation-state of the Jewish people, a rejection of Palestinian statehood, the maintenance of Israel's "security zones" in Syria, Lebanon and Gaza, and an arrangement on the issue of ultra-Orthodox conscription into the military through a "broad agreement" with the community's leaders.

headline: KCR To Return As CM In 2028, Claims KTR
content: BRS working president K.T. Rama Rao has said the countdown had begun for the Congress government and that the political scenario in Telangana would change within the next 500 days. He expressed confidence that BRS chief K. Chandrashekar Rao would return as chief minister in 2028. Addressing a Jana Chaitanya public meeting at the Kakatiya Degree College grounds in Hanamkonda on Sunday night, Rama Rao criticised the Revanth Reddy government and cited the projects brought to the city by the BRS government, including the Mega Textile Park, IT companies and a super-speciality hospital. He said the 2,250-bed hospital, spread across 24 floors, was awaiting completion and inauguration though 90 per cent of the work had been completed. Hospitals in Mahabubabad and Jangaon districts were also awaiting inauguration, he said. Rama Rao alleged that corruption was rampant under the Revanth Reddy government and branded it as a “20 per cent commission” regime. He accused the chief minister’s brothers of involvement in financial irregularities “ranging from `5 lakh crore to `10 lakh crore.” He said even Congress MLAs were speaking about the commission-based system. Rama Rao criticised changes being introduced in the education system, alleging that they were intended to serve the interests of certain individuals. Recalling the BRS government's 10-year tenure, Rama Rao said it had ensured uninterrupted power supply and continued welfare schemes even during the Covid-19 pandemic. He accused the Congress of misleading the people with 420 promises and failing to fulfill its assurances to women. The BRS leader criticised the government over its failure to bring water from Kannayapalli to the Devadula project. Rama Rao called on party workers to ensure a BRS victory in the next elections and welcomed several new members into the party. Ekashila educational institutions chairman Gauru Tirupathi Reddy from Warangal and several former corporators joined the BRS in his presence. ................ headline: He Found His Own Sugar Daddy: Shiv Sena UBT MP Priyanka Chaturvedi Takes Brutal Swipe At Yuzvendra Chahal
content: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Priyanka Chaturvedi took a sarcastic swipe at Indian cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal after news emerged of his political appointment in the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), triggering discussion on social media. Chaturvedi used the phrase 'sugar daddy' to mock Chahal following his appointment as a Special Invitee to the party's National Other Backward Classes (OBC) Morcha executive committee.Reacting to a post announcing Chahal's political role, Chaturvedi wrote on X (formerly Twitter) on November 21, 2026, "Seems like he found his own sugar daddy. IYKYK." Her remark quickly drew attention, with many interpreting it as a sarcastic reference to Chahal's personal life and the viral social media discourse surrounding him in recent years.Priyanka Chaturvedi Takes Dig At Yuzvendra Chahal After BJP AppointmentThe comment appeared to allude to the memes and online jokes involving Chahal, his former wife Dhanashree Verma, and the controversies that surfaced during their divorce proceedings. The phrase 'sugar daddy' became particularly significant in online discussions after Chahal was spotted wearing a T-shirt bearing the message 'Be your own sugar daddy', which subsequently became a talking point among social media users.Chaturvedi's remark, however, took the conversation in a political direction, coming immediately after Chahal's reported entry into the BJP's organisational structure. Her use of the phrase was widely perceived as an attempt to connect his political appointment with the earlier viral jokes surrounding his personal life.Chahal, who has made a name for himself as one of India's prominent leg-spinners across formats, has now found himself in the spotlight for reasons beyond cricket. His reported appointment in the BJP's OBC Morcha has attracted attention, with Chaturvedi's pointed remark adding another layer to the conversation around his transition into politics.The incident once again highlights how celebrity appointments in political organisations can quickly become fodder for online commentary, with personal references and viral memes often dominating the discussion. Chaturvedi's 'sugar daddy' remark has added a fresh twist to Chahal's latest headline-making development, shifting the spotlight from his cricketing career to his political association and the social media reaction surrounding it.Level up your brain the fun way.
